articles.title: A Review on Mechanisms of Action and Signaling Pathways of Natural Anti-hyperpigmentation Agents.
articles.abstract: Hyperpigmentation is a dermatological condition characterized by excessive melanin production, resulting in skin darkening. Intrinsic and extrinsic mediators, including ultraviolet (UV) radiation, hormonal changes, inflammation, and genetic predisposition, contribute to hyperpigmentation pathogenesis. The current review thoroughly examines the biological processes involved in hyperpigmentation, with particular emphasis on its signaling pathways, particularly the cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP), wingless-related integration site (Wnt)/β-catenin, phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt), and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), thereby providing mechanistic insights that may facilitate the development of effective treatments. The review also evaluates the safety, toxicity, and therapeutic efficacy of TYR inhibitors, arbutin, azelaic acid, ellagic acid, kojic acid, resveratrol, and the melanosome inhibitor niacinamide, for managing hyperpigmentation. Additionally, the review summarizes the in vitro and in vivo studies of these agents and other emerging plant extracts. Recent advances in the use of plant extracts for hyperpigmentation have shown promising efficacy; nevertheless, their translation into clinical and commercial applications remains limited. This limited translation might be attributed to the challenges related to standardization and the paucity of clinical evidence regarding long-term safety. Moreover, ongoing studies on natural anti-hyperpigmentation agents have highlighted the critical role of patent analyses in the advancement of biomedical research. This review provides a strategic direction for researchers to assess the safety, efficacy, and toxicity profiles of natural anti-hyperpigmentation agents.

articles.title: Phytopharmacological and Functional Insights Into the Bioactive Compounds of Grape (Vitis vinifera L.): An Integrated Review of In Vitro, In Vivo, and Clinical Studies.
articles.abstract: Grapes (Vitis vinifera L.) are abundant in polyphenols, flavonoids, and other bioactive constituents. They exhibit a wide range of health-promoting properties, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, anticancer, cardioprotective, antidiabetic, and skin anti-aging effects. We review and summarize the phytopharmacological and functional effects of grape-derived compounds. This review includes in vitro, in vivo, and clinical studies. The search combined the terms "V. vinifera" OR "grape" with keywords related to traditional uses, phytochemistry, and pharmacological activities. Peer-reviewed English-language studies published between 2000 and 2025 reporting ethnobotanical uses, phytochemical composition, or pharmacological effects were included. The findings were synthesized qualitatively. This review showed that grape seed and red grape extracts inhibited the growth of MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells. articles.title: Development of sericin-elastin nanoblends containing resveratrol for cosmeceutical applications.
articles.abstract: Resveratrol (RSV), a high-value phytocompound upcycled from winemaking byproducts, is highly promising for cosmeceutical applications against oxidative stress due to its extraordinary antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and cytoprotective properties. However, its topical application is severely limited by chemical instability, poor aqueous solubility, and rapid degradation by light and oxygen. To overcome these limitations and maximize epidermal efficacy, a biocompatible nanoblend composed of sericin and elastin was developed. The sericin (4 mg/mL)/elastin (2 mg/mL) nanoblends showed an average diameter of 140 nm, a narrow size distribution, a Zeta potential of -35 mV and high stability at pH 7 and 10, as well as at temperatures between 32 °C and 37 °C. The encapsulation of RSV (0.4 mg/mL) did not affect the mean diameter and polydispersity index of the systems, allowing an entrapment efficiency of ∼30% (drug content of 0.12 mg/mL). The release profile showed a biphasic kinetic trend over time. When tested on HaCaT human keratinocytes, both single polymers and blend nanosystems demonstrated excellent tolerability, confirming the high biocompatibility of the formulation. Furthermore, RSV-loaded blend nanoparticles showed a superior cytoprotective effect compared to the free drug, a trend confirmed by DPPH, CellROX and MitoSOX assays. Finally, CompuSyn analysis validated a strong synergy between the carrier and RSV (CI < 1) with a synergistic effect at 10 µg/mL with a Dose Reduction Index (DRI) of 3.00. In conclusion, the developed sericin-elastin nanoblends containing RSV represent innovative cosmeceuticals characterized by strong antioxidant activity able to be employed for the topical treatment of skin disorders.

articles.title: Resveratrol ameliorates acute kidney injury following burn injury by promoting mitophagy through SIRT5-mediated ATG3 succinylation.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a severe complication of burn trauma and is associated with significantly increased mortality. Resveratrol (RES) has shown therapeutic potential in AKI, yet its role in burn-induced AKI, particularly through the modulation of succinylation, remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of RES and the underlying molecular mechanisms in a burn-related AKI model. In vivo, AKI was induced in Sprague-Dawley rats by exposing the dorsal skin to boiling water, while in vitro, human kidney proximal tubular (HK2) cells were stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) to mimic inflammatory injury. The therapeutic efficacy of RES was assessed by measuring renal function parameters, inflammatory cytokine levels, and kidney injury biomarkers, supported by histopathological and ultrastructural examinations. In vitro, the effects of RES were evaluated through cell viability, apoptosis, and mitophagy assays. Mechanistic insights were obtained using molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), western blotting, immunoprecipitation (IP), and co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP). RES treatment significantly reduced blood urea nitrogen (BUN), serum creatinine (SCr), pro-inflammatory cytokines, and kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) levels, attenuated renal tubular damage, and improved mitochondrial and autophagosomal ultrastructure in burned rats. In LPS-stimulated HK2 cells, RES inhibited apoptosis and promoted mitophagy. Mechanistically, RES upregulated SIRT5 expression, which decreased global succinylation levels and enhanced ATG3 protein stability via K9 desuccinylation. Notably, ATG3 knockdown abrogated the renoprotective effects of RES in both in vivo and in vitro models. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that RES upregulates SIRT5 and inhibits ATG3 succinylation, thereby stabilizing ATG3 and promoting mitophagy, which collectively ameliorate burn-induced AKI.

articles.title: Next-generation risk assessment of resveratrol: An external exposure approach based on comprehensive read-across with independent internal exposure verification.
articles.abstract: Following the 2013 EU ban on animal testing for cosmetics, new approach methodologies (NAMs) have become essential. This study presents a next-generation risk assessment (NGRA) for resveratrol (RES) to demonstrate a framework where a primary external exposure approach is validated through an independent internal exposure challenge. Hypothetical scenarios for 1% RES in face cream and body lotion yielded systemic exposure doses exceeding the threshold of toxicological concern (TTC) levels. Consequently, a comprehensive read-across was conducted using structure-derived parameters and transcriptomic profiling (PCA and Wasserstein distance). Based on four identified stilbene analogs, a conservative surrogate NOAEL of 100 mg/kg/day was established, providing a margin of safety exceeding 100. Furthermore, internal exposure was evaluated using physiologically based kinetic (PBK) modeling. The predicted peak plasma concentrations (0.009 μM for face cream and 0.065 μM for body lotion) were well below the internal TTC of 1 μM. Additionally, margin of internal exposure based on a transcriptomic point of departure (2.4 μM) exceeded safety benchmarks. These consistent results demonstrate that cross-validating a primary external exposure approach with an independent internal challenge provides a high level of certainty in animal-free cosmetic safety assessments.

articles.title: Piceatannol enzymatically derived from resveratrol protects against UVB-induced skin injury by modulating antioxidant and inflammatory pathways.
articles.abstract: This study focused on optimising the tyrosinase-catalysed conversion of resveratrol (RES) to piceatannol (PCT) for efficient, low-cost production, as well as investigating the protective effects of PCT against UVB-induced skin damage. Conditions were optimised by adjusting temperature, enzyme concentration, pH, Vitamin C concentration, and reaction time. In HaCaT cell experiments, PCT provided greater cytoprotection than RES by improving cell survival, lowering UVB-induced ROS accumulation, increasing the activities of key antioxidant enzymes, and suppressing inflammatory mediators more effectively. articles.title: Dietary Modulation of microRNAs as a Potential Nutritional Strategy in Inflammatory and Autoimmune Skin Diseases: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Inflammatory and autoimmune skin diseases like psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, and hidradenitis suppurativa present significant therapeutic challenges due to their complex immunological and environmental pathogenesis. This review highlights the critical role of microRNAs (miRNAs) as epigenetic regulators of inflammatory processes and investigates the potential of nutrigenomics to modulate their expression. Bioactive dietary components-including polyphenols such as quercetin, resveratrol, and curcumin, alongside vitamins C and D, selenium, and omega-3 fatty acids-demonstrate the ability to alter miRNA profiles like miR-21, miR-146a, and miR-155. These miRNA alterations may contribute to the regulation of key inflammatory pathways, including nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-κB) and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), thereby potentially influencing pro-inflammatory cytokine production and keratinocyte proliferation. However, the extent to which individual dietary compounds directly mediate effects on these pathways through miRNA regulation varies and is often supported mainly by preclinical evidence. Clinical data suggests that dietary interventions, such as weight loss and the Mediterranean diet alleviate skin symptoms and lower systemic inflammatory markers. Identifying disease-specific miRNA expression profiles represents an emerging research avenue that may, following analytical and clinical validation, inform future approaches in dermatology.

articles.abstract: Polyphenols have been investigated in dental materials and restorative techniques due to their interactions with metal cations, antioxidant activity, and collagen crosslinking ability, which make them a promise for reinforcing the dental substrate and improving material adhesion. However, more studies are necessary before to support their use in clinical procedures.

articles.title: An oral coral-like resveratrol nanocomplex protects against dry eye disease through ocular and systemic redox homeostasis.
articles.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a progressive ocular disorder in which chronic inflammation and oxidative stress synergistically damage ocular tissues and impair vision. While topical anti-inflammatory and artificial tears therapies are the standard treatment for DED, their long-term application is limited by adverse effects and poor patient compliance. Emerging evidence suggests that systemic redox dysregulation contributes to DED pathogenesis, highlighting the potential of oral antioxidant intervention as a disease-modifying strategy. However, the clinical translation of oral antioxidants has been constrained by poor bioavailability and rapid metabolic clearance. Herein, a coral-like resveratrol nanocomplex was fabricated with a composite natural carrier of sericin and dipotassium glycyrrhizinate through a simple pH-ultrasonic-shifting method in aqueous solution, enabling effective oral delivery of this potent polyphenolic antioxidant. This coral-like nanocomplex markedly enhanced gastrointestinal stability and systemic exposure of resveratrol, increasing oral bioavailability by approximately 6.62-fold and ocular accumulation by 2.49-fold. The nanocomplex exerted robust ocular and systemic antioxidant effects and protected against experimental DED in mice. Oral administration of this nanocomplex protected against benzalkonium chloride (BAC)-induced corneal epithelial damage, tear film dysfunction, and inflammatory responses. Mechanistically, the nanocomplex alleviated oxidative damage through ocular and systemic redox homeostasis. Rather than acting solely on the ocular surface, this orally nanomedicine may provide complementary therapeutic benefits through ocular and systemic redox regulation, while also being associated with modulation of gut microbiota and metabolic profiles. These findings support oral redox intervention as a promising complementary strategy for protecting against the DED, particularly for reducing the burden of prolonged topical treatment.
